source.title: 2 AI Coding Strategies I Wish I Knew Earlier
source.author: Cody Seibert (Web Dev Cody)

summary: Short YouTube reflection by Cody Seibert (Automaker creator) articulating a single decision axis for agent coding: well-known requirements (use plan mode with 1-5 iterations) vs uncertain requirements (rapid pair-prompting with multiple parallel agent windows, no MD file upfront). Introduces a spike-then-harden pivot pattern: use vibe iteration to discover the real requirements, then stash everything and restart in plan mode for production quality. Explicit admission that iterative mode accumulates slop.
key_patterns: Requirements-uncertainty gate — single-axis decision rule at task intake
Plan mode + 1-5 iteration loops with question-asking as edge-case surfacer
TDD/Cypress as in-implementation guardrails for the 5-20% plan-miss rate
Pair-prompting on Zoom with UX/product co-driver instead of spec docs
Multiple parallel agent windows during play-test (one agent per observed bug)
Spike-then-harden: stash prototype code, restart in plan mode once requirements are known
Explicit slop-accumulation cost of iterative mode (discovery-only)
unusual_workflows: Parallel agent windows spawned reactively during play-test (not pre-planned) — maps directly to our tmux+worktree model but applied to live UX testing rather than issue queue processing
Stash-and-restart: discarding working prototype code to re-implement in plan mode is counterintuitive but named explicitly as a code-quality move
